title: Nuclear magnetic resonance therapy for deep-tissue biophysical stimulation: an integrated clinical and molecular analysis.
first_affiliation: Poliklinika K-CENTAR, Vrbik 8 a, 10000 Zagreb, Croatia.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION OR BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Musculoskeletal disorders such as osteoarthritis, chronic low back pain, radicular syndromes, and osteoporosis require noninvasive treatments reaching deep anatomical structures. Nuclear magnetic resonance therapy (NMRT/MBST) delivers depth-independent resonance-based stimulation. This systematic review consolidates clinical and mechanistic evidence to evaluate NMRT/MBST among deep-tissue biophysical therapeutics.

abstract.label: SOURCES OF DATA
abstract.text: A systematic search of PubMed, Ovid/Embase, and peer-reviewed literature identified 26 original studies spanning randomized and observational clinical evidence, imaging evaluations, veterinary trials, and in vitro research. Experimental findings on inflammatory, metabolic, mitochondrial, redox, and circadian pathways were integrated with clinical observations.

abstract.label: AREAS OF AGREEMENT
abstract.text: NMRT/MBST shows a strong safety profile with no reported treatment-emergent adverse events. Across indications, studies demonstrate improvements in pain, function, and, selectively, structural or densitometric changes. Mechanistic evidence indicates modulation of mitochondrial bioenergetics, redox balance, inflammatory cascades, chondrogenic and osteogenic pathways, neurotrophic activity, and circadian regulation. These convergent processes mirror photobiomodulation, supporting NMRT/MBST as a deep-acting analog influencing regenerative biology in inaccessible tissues. Conventional pulsed electromagnetic field therapy is physically the closest comparator but shows narrower mechanistic overlap.

abstract.label: AREAS OF CONTROVERSY
abstract.text: Evidence remains heterogeneous in methodology, outcome measures, and structural responses. The only placebo-controlled knee osteoarthritis trial found no superiority over sham, although baseline imbalance limits interpretation.

abstract.label: GROWING POINTS
abstract.text: The depth-independent profile and mechanistic parallels suggest applications in deep cartilage, subchondral bone, intervertebral discs, and nerve-root environments, supporting multimodal biophysical strategies.

abstract.label: AREAS TIMELY FOR DEVELOPING RESEARCH
abstract.text: Priorities include larger randomized trials, longitudinal structural evaluation, comparisons with optical modalities, and biomarker-guided personalization.

title: Effect of zinc oxide nanoparticles and light-emitting diode radiation on the viability and differentiation of stem cell derived from human apical papilla.
first_affiliation: Department of Endodontics, Faculty of Dentistry, Dental Research Center, Hamadan University of Medical Sciences, Hamadan, Iran.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnONPs) have shown potential in regenerative medicine, particularly when combined with light-emitting diode (LED) radiation. This study aimed to explore the effects of ZnONPs combined with LED radiation on human stem cells derived from the apical papilla (HSCAPs), focusing on primary outcomes of cell viability, odontoblast-like differentiation, and mineralization.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This in vitro experimental study utilized ZnONPs synthesized via a green method using pomegranate peel extract. HSCAPs were divided into four groups: control, ZnONPs-only, LED-only, and ZnONPs + LED (experimental group). Cell viability, a primary outcome, was assessed using the MTT (3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide) assay at 24 h. Odontogenic and osteogenic differentiation, evaluated through dentin sialophosphoprotein (DSPP), bone sialoprotein (BSP), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), and dentin matrix acidic phosphoprotein 1 (DMP1) gene expression using qRT-PCR, were assessed on day 7. Mineralization, determined through Alizarin Red S staining, was measured on day 14. The doses used were 1 μg/mL ZnONPs and 620-640 nm range, 85% total emission LED radiation at 5 mW/cm2 for 30 s, the energy density would be 6 Joules/cm2. Statistical analyses were performed using Kruskal-Wallis and dunn's post hoc tests. (P < 0.05).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Cell viability was highest at 1 μg/mL ZnONPs, comparable to control (p > 0.05), and decreased at higher concentrations (p < 0.05). Odontogenic and osteogenic gene expression, including DSPP, ALP, BSP and DMP1was significantly upregulated (p < 0.05) in the ZnONPs + LED group compared to all other groups. Alizarin Red S staining revealed the densest mineralization in the ZnONPs + LED group, followed by LED-only and ZnONPs-only groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The synergistic application of ZnONPs and LED irradiation significantly enhanced odontogenic and osteogenic differentiation and mineralization of HSCAPs, suggesting their potential utility in endodontic regenerative therapies.

title: Physiotherapeutic and technological approaches to lumbar disc herniation per sustainable development goal 3: Scoping Review.
journal: JPMA. The Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association
first_affiliation: Department of Allied Health Sciences, The superior University, Lahore, Pakistan.
keywords: Lumbar disc herniation, Physical therapy modalities, Rehabilitation, Pain, Telemedicine.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To map current physiotherapeutic and technological interventions for lumbar disc herniation, and to evaluate their alignment with Sustainable Development Goal-3.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The scoping review was conducted at Department of Allied Health The Superior University from January 2025 to June 2025 and comprised literature search on PubMed, Scopus, Physiotherapy Evidence Database, Cochrane Library, Directory of Open Access Journals, PakMediNet and Google Scholar databases for randomised controlled trials published between January 2015 and June 2025 about physiotherapeutic or technology-assisted interventions in lumbar disc herniation(LDH) patients which reported clinical outcomes. Data was extracted and subjected to narrative synthesis.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of the 78 studies assessed, 15(19.2%) randomised controlled trials (RCTs) including 1,261 participants aged 18-80 years were analysed. Physiotherapeutic interventions(n=10) including manual therapy, spinal mobilisation, McKenzie and motor control exercises, Pilates and combination approaches, demonstrated consistent improvements in pain, disability, functional outcomes and quality of life. Adjunctive modalities, such as bamboo-based medicinal moxibustion, traction with paraffinotherapy, and neurodynamic mobilisation further improved functional outcomes or neuropathic symptoms. Technologyassisted interventions(n=5) including non-surgical spinal decompression, portable lumbar exoskeletons, digital app-based physiotherapy, Quick Response code-guided exercise programmes and high-intensity laser therapy, produced comparable improvements to conventional physiotherapy, with additional benefits in treatment adherence and patient satisfaction.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Both conventional physiotherapy and selected technology-assisted interventions were associated with improvements in pain, disability and functional outcomes in lumbar disc herniation patients.

title: Effect of Photobiomodulation Applied to Masticatory Muscle Tender Points Combined With the Rocabado Approach in Patients With Myogenic Temporomandibular Disorders: A Double-Blind, Randomized Controlled Trial.
first_affiliation: Faculty of Physical Therapy, Department of Physical Therapy for Musculoskeletal Disorders and its Surgeries, MISR University for Science and Technology, 6th of October City, Egypt.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Temporomandibular Joint Disorder (TMD) is a complex condition of multifactorial aetiology. Consequently, numerous studies have investigated optimal treatment strategies, with several reporting that multimodal approaches can effectively enhance pain relief and mandibular mobility.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: To investigate the effect of adding Photobiomodulation (PBM) to the Rocabado approach on pain intensity, pain threshold, mouth opening, and TMJ function in patients with myogenic TMDs.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Fifty-two patients of both genders, from 18 to 40 years old, with myogenic TMDs were randomly assigned either to the PBM group or the placebo group. The PBM group (n = 26) received active PBM in addition to the Rocabado approach, while the control group (n = 26) received placebo PBM in addition to the Rocabado approach. All patients received 3 sessions a week for 6 weeks. Clinical assessment, including pain pressure threshold, pain intensity, maximum mouth opening, and TMJ function were assessed for all participants before and after the treatment program.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Fifty-two participants completed the study. Both groups showed significant within-group improvements across all outcomes (p < 0.05). Post-treatment, the Photobiomodulation group showed significantly greater improvements than the placebo group in pressure pain thresholds across all tested masticatory muscle sites (p < 0.05). Furthermore, the Photobiomodulation group achieved superior outcomes in mouth opening ROM (MD = 5.84 mm, 95% CI: 3.06 to 8.63, p = 0.001), pain intensity reduction (MD = -1.81, 95% CI: -2.46 to -1.02, p = 0.013), and TMJ functional scores: TMDDI (MD = -24.97, 95% CI: -32.72 to -18.39, p = 0.001), TMDSIS (MD = -16.83, 95% CI: -22.64 to -11.17, p = 0.001), and TMDSFS (MD = -14.98, 95% CI: -21.67 to -11.82, p = 0.001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Photobiomodulation combined with the Rocabado approach is more effective than the Rocabado approach alone in improving pain intensity, pain threshold, maximum mouth opening, and TMJ function in patients with myogenic TMDs. All procedures were performed in accordance with the 1964 Declaration of Helsinki and its later amendments. This study was registered in the ClinicalTrials.gov registry, registration number: NCT07026617.

title: Three-dimensional alveolar ridge augmentation combined with photobiomodulation therapy for post-traumatic bone loss: clinical protocol, case report, and evidence review.
first_affiliation: Department of Periodontics, Bo.C., Islamic Azad University, Borujerd, Islamic Republic of Iran. derikvand1@iau.ac.ir.

abstract.text: Post-traumatic alveolar ridge deficiencies often involve three-dimensional bone loss, making dental implant placement highly challenging. Guided bone regeneration techniques, combined with fixation devices, soft tissue substitutes, and adjunctive photobiomodulation therapy, have been proposed to enhance predictability and clinical outcomes. A 46-year-old female with severe alveolar bone loss, insufficient keratinized tissue, and maxillary sinus pneumatization following trauma was treated. Simultaneous three-dimensional ridge augmentation was performed using cortical cancellous Regen Allograft stabilized with bone plates and tenting screws. An open sinus lift was carried out with graft placement beneath the elevated Schneiderian membrane and coverage with a collagen membrane. Soft tissue management included palatal tissue mobilization and placement of acellular dermal matrix (Regen Allograft) under the flap. Postoperative photobiomodulation therapy was applied using an 808 nm diode laser (0.2 W, 4 J/cm²) to enhance soft and hard tissue healing. After six months of healing, six implants (IRES, volution, SVB) were placed under guided surgery, followed by screw-retained prosthetic rehabilitation. Clinical and CBCT examinations were performed during a 24-month follow-up period. CBCT evaluation at six months demonstrated sufficient horizontal and vertical bone regeneration, enabling successful placement of six implants with satisfactory primary stability. Soft tissue healing progressed uneventfully, with favorable tissue maturation and minimal postoperative discomfort. Prosthetic rehabilitation was completed successfully, and clinical and radiographic follow-up over 24 months revealed stable peri-implant bone levels, healthy peri implant soft tissues, satisfactory esthetic and functional outcomes, and no biological or mechanical complications. This case demonstrates that combining bone grafting with fixation devices, sinus augmentation, acellular dermal matrix, and photobiomodulation can successfully manage complex post-traumatic ridge deficiencies. The multidisciplinary approach provided predictable functional and esthetic outcomes.

title: Effect of High-Power Laser Acupuncture on Fatigue and Proprioception in Chronic Nonspecific Low Back Pain: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
first_affiliation: Department of Medical Rehabilitation Sciences, College of Applied Medical Sciences, Najran University, Najran, Saudi Arabia.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To examine the effects of adding high-power laser acupuncture (HPLA) to an exercise program on back muscular fatigability and endurance, lumbar proprioception, pain severity, and pain-related self-efficacy in chronic nonspecific low back pain (CNLBP) patients.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Sixty adults with CNLBP aged 20-40 years enrolled in this double-blind, randomized sham-controlled trial with equal and random assignment to receive HPLA plus exercise therapy or sham laser plus the same exercise therapy three times weekly over a six-week period. Back muscle fatigue and lumbar proprioception were assessed by an isokinetic dynamometer; endurance by the Biering-Sørensen test; pain severity by the visual analog scale; and pain-related self-efficacy using the Arabic Pain Self-Efficacy Questionnaire. Evaluations were carried out both before and just after the six-week intervention.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Within-group analyses demonstrated significant improvements across all outcomes in each group. Between-group analyses revealed significantly greater improvements in the HPLA treatment group across all measured variables (P < 0.05). At post-intervention, the HPLA group demonstrated a greater number of repetitions to fatigue (mean difference [MD] = 7.10 repetitions; 95% CI: 3.42 to 10.78) and lower lumbar proprioceptive error (MD = -1.27°; 95% CI: -1.60 to -0.93) compared with the sham group.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In cases of CNLBP, adding HPLA as an adjunct to exercise therapy may improve back muscle fatigue, endurance, lumbar proprioception, pain severity, and pain self-efficacy over a six-week intervention period. However, these short-term improvements require confirmation through longitudinal follow-up studies. Future research should emphasise dose response and long-term effects.

title: Red Light Therapy and Mitochondrial Rejuvenation in Age-Related Disorders.
first_affiliation: The Student Scientific Society, Poznan University of Medical Sciences, 60-806, Poznan, Poland.

abstract.text: Aging is associated with mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired ATP production, and a decline in tissue regenerative capacity, leading to the development of age-related diseases. This review summarizes current evidence regarding the effects of photobiomodulation (PBM) on mitochondrial function and age-related disorders. PBM using red and near-infrared light may enhance proper mitochondrial function by acting on cytochrome c oxidase (CCO) and other signaling pathways, including the transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) channel, leading to increased ATP production, modulation of ROS signaling, and improved cellular homeostasis. We review in vitro, animal, and clinical studies investigating PBM in metabolic, neurodegenerative, hepatic, cardiovascular, age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and skeletal muscle disorders associated with aging, as well as its application in the management of cancer therapy-related oral mucositis. Current studies demonstrate beneficial effects on glucose metabolism, cardiovascular function, neuronal function, lipid metabolism, liver function, muscle regeneration, and visual function in AMD, as well as the safety and efficacy of PBM in the management of cancer therapy-induced oral mucositis. The therapeutic effects of PBM appear to be dose-dependent and influenced by treatment parameters including wavelength, fluence, irradiance, and exposure protocol. Although photobiomodulation still lacks standardized treatment protocols and differences exist in the wavelengths used, dosage, and frequency among studies, it represents a promising therapeutic approach for the treatment of age-related diseases.

title: Red and near-infrared photobiomodulation in precision medicine: mechanisms, dosimetry, and clinical translation.
first_affiliation: Medical Equipment Department, Affiliated Hospital of Jining Medical University, Jining, Shandong, China.

abstract.text: Phototherapy is a non-invasive therapeutic modality that uses specific wavelengths of light to modulate biological processes and treat disease. Driven by advances in photobiology, regenerative medicine, and clinical technology, phototherapy has evolved from empirical heliotherapy into a mechanism-based intervention with expanding medical applications. This review places the biological effects, therapeutic indications, and safety profiles of ultraviolet, blue, and green light in comparative context, while focusing primarily on the mechanisms, dosimetry, and clinical translation of red and near-infrared photobiomodulation (PBM). Although ultraviolet and blue light therapies have established roles in dermatology and neonatal jaundice, their clinical use is limited by concerns such as photocarcinogenesis, retinal phototoxicity, and circadian disruption. In contrast, red and near-infrared light offer deeper tissue penetration and, when appropriately dosed, a comparatively low risk of direct photochemical injury. Through mitochondrial, redox, inflammatory, and other context-dependent signaling pathways, red/NIR PBM has been investigated in wound repair, chronic pain, osteoarthritis, musculoskeletal disorders, neurological conditions, and dermatological applications. As a representative quantitative example, a 2024 meta-analysis of 10 placebo-controlled randomized trials involving 542 participants with knee osteoarthritis found a moderate reduction in pain at rest with PBM compared with placebo (standardized mean difference, - 0.70; 95% confidence interval, - 1.10 to - 0.20), although the certainty of evidence was very low. However, broader clinical translation remains constrained by heterogeneous dosimetry, insufficiently standardized treatment protocols, and uneven evidence maturity across indications. To address these limitations, we propose a precision-oriented framework that links clinical target, tissue-optical context, wavelength selection, patient- and site-specific modifiers, dosimetric implications, measurable endpoints, and evidence maturity. This framework is intended to support treatment planning, parameter reporting, and prospective validation rather than to prescribe currently validated individualized dosing algorithms.

title: Photobiomodulation versus stabilization splint, both combined with self-management, for acute temporomandibular myalgia: 48-week outcomes of a partially randomized controlled study.
first_affiliation: Ha Noi Medical University, Hanoi, Vietnam.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Photobiomodulation (LLLT) is used for myogenous temporomandibular disorders (TMD), but longer-term comparative evidence versus stabilization splints alongside structured self-management remains limited. This study aims to compare pain reduction and maximum painless mouth opening after photobiomodulation+self-management (PBM + SM) versus stabilization splint+self-management (OS + SM), with an additional self-management-only comparator (SM), over 48 weeks.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This partially randomized controlled study enrolled 66 patients with DC/TMD-diagnosed acute masticatory muscle pain. Forty-four participants consenting to intervention were randomized 1:1 to PBM + SM (660-nm diode laser, twice weekly, 10 sessions) or OS + SM (maxillary stabilization splint worn at night, 8 h/day for 2 months). Both intervention groups received the same SM programme (education, habit modification, and jaw exercises for 2 months). A non-randomized convenience group received SM alone (n = 22). Assessments were performed at baseline and weeks 2, 4, 12, 24, and 48. Primary outcomes were VAS pain (0-10) and maximum painless mouth opening (MPMO, mm). Secondary outcomes included masticatory muscle tenderness and Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC). Longitudinal analyses used linear mixed-effects models.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: All groups improved over time, with earlier improvement in both intervention arms. In the randomized comparison, PBM + SM and OS + SM showed comparable week-48 outcomes for VAS pain and MPMO. No significant between-group difference in masticatory muscle tender points was observed at week 48 after Holm adjustment. Comparisons involving the SM-only group were exploratory.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Over 48 weeks, PBM + SM and OS + SM produced comparable improvements in pain and maximum painless mouth opening, with no significant between-group difference in masticatory muscle tender points at week 48.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT06419738.

title: Therapeutic Ultrasound for Pain Management in Temporomandibular Disorders: A Systematic Review of Clinical Evidence From Controlled and Prospective Studies.
first_affiliation: Department of Pain Medicine, Taihe Hospital, Hubei University of Medicine, Shiyan, Hubei, 442000, China.

abstract.text: Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) are a common source of persistent orofacial pain and are estimated to affect a substantial proportion of the population. Therapeutic ultrasound is a non-invasive modality frequently used in musculoskeletal rehabilitation, although its clinical effectiveness for TMD-related pain remains debated. This systematic review was designed and reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 recommendations. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from database inception to April 2026. We included randomized controlled trials, prospective clinical studies, and comparative clinical designs evaluating therapeutic ultrasound for pain management in adults with TMDs. The primary outcomes were pain intensity, assessed using VAS, NRS, or VRS, and mandibular function, assessed mainly by mouth opening. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool for randomized trials and ROBINS-I for non-randomized studies. Because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively rather than pooled statistically. The search identified 143 records, of which 82 remained after duplicate removal and were screened. Thirty-seven full-text articles were assessed, and 23 studies involving 1256 participants (1226 of them with a temporomandibular disorder) met the eligibility criteria. Twenty-one of 23 studies reported a statistically significant reduction in pain relative to their own baseline; however, these are within-group changes rather than treatment effects, and the certainty of the evidence for pain reduction was very low (GRADE), with low certainty for mandibular function, pressure pain threshold and quality of life/disability. Reported reductions included VAS improvement from 42 to 18 when ultrasound was added to home exercise, compared with 40-26 with exercise alone, and VAS improvement from 4.90 to 1.70 after low-intensity ultrasound therapy in a large randomized trial. Compared with low-level laser therapy or photobiomodulation, four studies favored laser-based treatment, whereas one study favored low-intensity ultrasound combined with exercise. Ultrasound was superior to TENS in two studies, while one study found no meaningful difference among ultrasound, TENS, and LLLT. No consistent difference was observed between continuous and pulsed ultrasound modes. Among randomized trials, 8 studies were judged as low risk of bias, 8 raised some concerns, and 1 was judged as high risk of bias. Adverse events were reported by only 2 of the 23 studies, so the safety of the intervention could not be characterised. Therapeutic ultrasound may reduce pain and improve mandibular function in patients with temporomandibular disorders, particularly as an adjunct to multimodal rehabilitation; however, the certainty of the evidence is very low for pain and low for mandibular function, pressure pain threshold and quality of life/disability, and the optimal treatment parameters remain undetermined. These findings should not be interpreted as establishing clinical efficacy. Although some comparative studies reported greater pain reduction with LLLT/PBM than with ultrasound, this finding should be interpreted cautiously because the number of studies was small and treatment protocols were heterogeneous. Therefore, current evidence does not establish the superiority of LLLT/PBM over therapeutic ultrasound.

title: A comparative study of low-level laser therapy combined with drugs versus drug therapy alone in the management of myogenic TMJ pain.
first_affiliation: UNIVERSITY OF BAGHDAD, BAGHDAD, IRAQ.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: Aim: To compare the effect of low-level laser therapy combined with pharmacotherapy (naproxen + orphenadrine with paracetamol (myogesic)) and pharmacotherapy alone in treating myofascial pain related to temporomandibular joint.

abstract.label: PATIENTS AND METHODS
abstract.text: Materials and Methods: Twenty-four participants with myofascial pain related to TMJ diagnosed according to diagnostic criteria DC/TMJ are randomly divided into two groups (n=12); Group1 received naproxen 500mg twice a day and myogesic three times a day for 21 days, Group 2 received Low-Level Laser Therapy for nine sessions three sessions a week with a diode laser with dual-wavelength with the same drugs as group1. Measures of myofascial pain during the function were evaluated at baseline, after 10 days, at the end of treatment, and 3 months after the end of treatments using the visual analog scale VAS, which has scores from zero (no pain) to ten (sever pain) also maximum mouth opening was measured in each session.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Results: VAS scores decreased in both groups but significantly more in Low-Level Laser Therapy with pharmacotherapy group at 10 days, 21 days, and 3 months (p < 0.05). Maximum mouth opening highly improved in Group 2 with significantly more significant gains in Low-Level Laser Therapy group at all follow-up points except baseline (p < 0.05).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Conclusions: These results indicate that Low-Level Laser Therapy with pharmacotherapy was more effective than pharmacological therapy in decreasing pain and improving jaw function in patients with TMJ-related myogenic pain.

title: Short-term effects of extracorporeal shockwave therapy and low-level laser therapy on clinical outcomes and ultrasonographic tendon thickness in lateral elbow tendinopathy.
journal: Journal of back and musculoskeletal rehabilitation
first_affiliation: Department of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation, Hitit University Faculty of Medicine, Çorum, Turkey.

abstract.text: BackgroundThis study aimed to compare the short-term effects of extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) and low-level laser therapy (LLLT) on pain, elbow function, health-related quality of life, hand grip strength, and ultrasonographic extensor tendon thickness in patients with LET.ObjectiveIn this prospective, randomized, controlled, single-blind trial, patients with LET were randomly assigned to either ESWT or LLLT. Both groups received the same standardized home exercise program and lateral epicondylitis brace. Visual Analog Scale (VAS), the Patient-Rated Tennis Elbow Evaluation (PRTEE), Short Form-36 (SF-36), hand grip strength, and ultrasonographic evaluation were assessed before and after three weeks of randomisation.ResultsAt three weeks, the ESWT group demonstrated significantly lower post-treatment pain intensity (VAS) than the LLLT group (p = 0.004). ESWT was also associated with significantly better outcomes in PRTEE pain scores (p = 0.030), ultrasonographic tendon thickness (p = 0.021), and the Role Physical (p = 0.029) and General Health (p = 0.005) domains of the SF-36. No significant between-group differences were observed in hand grip strength, PRTEE function, PRTEE total score, or the remaining SF-36 domains.ConclusionWhen used as adjuncts to a standardized exercise program and LET brace, ESWT was associated with greater short-term pain reduction and more favorable outcomes in the PRTEE pain subscale, ultrasonographic tendon thickness, and selected domains of health-related quality of life compared with LLLT. These findings suggest that ESWT may offer greater short-term pain-related benefits than LLLT when both are added to exercise and bracing.

title: 630 nm light-emitting diode irradiation suppresses inflammation and promotes osteoblast differentiation in periodontal cell models - in vitro study.
first_affiliation: BioMedical Sciences Graduate Program (BMSGP), Chonnam National University, Hwasun, Jeollanam-do, Republic of Korea.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Periodontal disease involves persistent inflammation and alveolar bone loss. Photobiomodulation using light-emitting diodes (LEDs) may regulate inflammation and bone remodelling, but the optimal wavelength and irradiation timing remain unclear.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Human gingival fibroblasts and RAW 264.7 macrophages were irradiated with 525, 630, or 850 nm LED light before or after lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation. The effects of 630 nm irradiation were further evaluated in primary mouse calvarial osteoblasts, MC3T3-E1 cells, bone marrow-derived macrophages, and RAW 264.7 osteoclast precursors. Inflammatory mediators, nitric oxide production, cell viability, osteoblast differentiation, and osteoclast formation were assessed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among the wavelengths tested, 630 nm irradiation most consistently reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine expression and secretion and decreased nitric oxide production without affecting cell viability. In primary osteoblasts and MC3T3-E1 cells, 630 nm irradiation at 5 and 10 J/cm² increased alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, osteogenic marker expression, RUNX2 protein levels, and Smad1/5/9 phosphorylation. In contrast, the same irradiation conditions did not significantly affect osteoclast differentiation or the expression of osteoclast-related markers.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Irradiation with 630 nm LED light suppressed inflammatory responses and promoted osteoblast differentiation without enhancing osteoclastogenesis. These findings suggest that 630 nm photobiomodulation may provide a balanced therapeutic approach for periodontal disease, although further validation in animal models and clinical studies is required.

title: Combined effects of photobiomodulation and platelet-rich plasma on healing of acute Achilles tendon injuries in rats.
first_affiliation: Department of Pain Medicine, Nanjing Jinling Hospital, Affiliated Hospital of Medical School, Nanjing University, Nanjing, China.

abstract.text: Tendon injuries are challenging to treat due to limited intrinsic healing, and although photobiomodulation (PBM) and platelet-rich plasma (PRP) show therapeutic potential, their combined effects remain unclear. This study evaluated the individual and combined efficacy of PBM and PRP on Achilles tendon repair in rats. A total of 144 rats were assigned to six groups and treated with PBM, PRP, or combined PBM + PRP therapy; tissues were collected at 1 and 8 weeks for biochemical and histological assessment. Both PBM and PRP reduced IL-1β and TNF-α levels and improved collagen organization, while the combined therapy produced the most pronounced anti-inflammatory response and structural recovery. Notably, PBM + PRP significantly enhanced and prolonged PDGF-BB expression compared with either treatment alone. These findings demonstrate that PBM and PRP each promote tendon healing, but their combination yields superior therapeutic benefits through amplified modulation of inflammatory and regenerative pathways, highlighting their potential as an improved therapeutic strategy.

title: Thermographic outcomes of auricular laser acupuncture and auricular seed acupressure in older adults with chronic shoulder pain: an exploratory nonrandomized, nonconcurrent comparison.
first_affiliation: Postgraduate Program in Biomedical Engineering, Universidade do Vale do Paraíba (UNIVAP), São José dos Campos, Brazil. gersonquadros@yahoo.com.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Compare pain, quality of life, and cutaneous temperature changes within predefined anterior, lateral, and posterior shoulder regions of interest between auricular laser acupuncture and seed acupressure in older adults with chronic shoulder pain.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This exploratory, nonrandomized, open-label study enrolled 20 adults aged 60-90 years, allocated by order of entry to consecutive, nonconcurrent cohorts of auricular laser acupuncture (n = 10) or seed acupressure (n = 10), treated twice weekly for five weeks. VAS, McGill, SF-36, and thermography were assessed before the first (A1) and fifth sessions (A2) and after the tenth (A3) and analyzed using linear mixed-effects models.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: From A1 to A3, VAS decreased by - 2.70 points in Laser (95% CI - 4.37 to - 1.03) and - 2.50 in Seed (95% CI - 4.17 to - 0.83); the between-group difference was - 0.20 points (Laser - Seed; 95% CI - 2.54 to 2.14). Selected McGill and SF-36 outcomes changed; McGill affective A1-to-A2 change differed between groups (Laser - Seed: -2.70; 95% CI - 4.86 to - 0.55; p = 0.017). Anterior thermal range (ΔT) showed a TIME × GROUP interaction (p = 0.007); the A1-to-A3 between-group difference was - 1.941 °C (Seed - Laser; 95% CI - 3.097 to - 0.785), although Seed ΔT was higher at baseline (+ 1.496 °C; 95% CI 0.607 to 2.385). Lateral ΔT showed a TIME effect (p = 0.033); posterior ΔT showed none.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Clinical outcomes improved over time without evidence of differential changes between interventions. Thermography identified region-specific ΔT trajectories, warranting further investigation as a complementary method.

abstract.label: CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07010627.

title: Comparative efficacy of extracorporeal shockwave therapy versus low-level laser therapy for myogenous temporomandibular disorders: a randomised controlled trial protocol.
first_affiliation: Department of Rehabilitation Medicine, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine Affiliated Ninth People's Hospital, Shanghai, China.

abstract.label: INTRODUCTION
abstract.text: Myogenous temporomandibular disorders (mTMDs) are common chronic orofacial pain conditions associated with restricted mandibular function and impaired quality of life. Low-level laser therapy (LLLT) is widely used as a conservative, non-invasive treatment, but its clinical application is limited by high treatment frequency, heterogeneous dosage parameters and inconsistent evidence regarding long-term efficacy. Extracorporeal shockwave therapy (ESWT) is an emerging non-invasive modality that may provide stable analgesic effects with fewer treatment sessions. However, direct head-to-head randomised controlled trials comparing ESWT and LLLT in patients with mTMD are lacking.

abstract.label: METHODS AND ANALYSIS
abstract.text: This single-centre, parallel-group, open-label randomised controlled trial with blinded outcome assessors and statisticians will enrol 68 patients with mTMD (diagnostic criteria (DC)/TMD axis I, aged 18–65 years, baseline Visual Analogue Scale (VAS)-open ≥3). Participants will be randomly allocated (1:1) to receive either ESWT (one session/week for 4 weeks) or LLLT (three sessions/week for 4 weeks), both combined with standardised health education. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, the end of treatment (week 4), and at 3-month and 6-month follow-ups. The primary outcome is the change in VAS-open from baseline to week 4. Statistical analyses will follow the intention-to-treat principle. The primary treatment effect at week 4 will be evaluated using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), adjusting for baseline VAS-open. Longitudinal changes will be analysed using linear mixed-effects models including treatment group, time and group-by-time interaction. Two-sided tests will be used with α=0.05.

abstract.label: ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION
abstract.text: Ethical approval was granted by the Institutional Review Board of Shanghai Ninth People’s Hospital (approval No. SH9H-2024-T502-3). All participants will provide written informed consent. The results will be submitted for publication.

title: Laser as an Adjunct in Endodontic Treatment in Dogs: Perspectives on a Conservative, Effective, and Safe Approach.
first_affiliation: Faculty of Veterinary Medicine and Animal Science, University of São Paulo, São Paulo, Brazil.

abstract.text: Crown fractures and subsequent pulp necrosis are common clinical findings in veterinary dental practice. While conventional endodontic therapy typically yields favorable outcomes, light therapies, such as antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT) and photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT), have emerged as promising adjuncts for enhancing disinfection and tissue repair. However, standardized protocols for these therapies in veterinary dentistry remain scarce. This clinical case report describes the management of a maxillary incisor with pulp necrosis secondary to a coronal fracture in a dog. Following conventional chemomechanical preparation, aPDT was performed using 0.01% methylene blue as a photosensitizer and a 660 nm diode laser (100 mW, 9 J) delivered via an intracanal diffusing fiber. Immediately after the endodontic canal manipulation, the diode laser (PBMT; 808 nm, 3 J/point) was applied using contact transmucosal mode to modulate inflammation and stimulate periapical bone repair, followed by weekly sessions for 3 weeks. Radiographic and clinical follow-up at day 1, 2 and 8 weeks, and 1 year postoperatively demonstrated progressive alveolar healing and the absence of clinical symptoms. The combined use of aPDT and PBMT with the described laser parameters seemed to be a promising, conservative and effective approach to optimize root canal disinfection, promoting local analgesy and possible accelerating apical bone remodeling. The results suggest that light therapies are valuable tools for enhancing endodontic success in dogs.

title: Photobiomodulation therapy for the management of pain associated with temporomandibular disorders: a systematic review.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To determine whether photobiomodulation (PBM; formerly low-level laser therapy) reduces temporomandibular disorder (TMD) pain relative to a concurrent comparator, to report the evidence by diagnostic stratum, and to appraise its certainty and dosimetric reporting.

abstract.label: STUDY SELECTION
abstract.text: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from January 2016 to July 2026 for controlled clinical trials of PBM for TMD-related pain in participants diagnosed by RDC/TMD or DC/TMD criteria. The review followed PRISMA 2020 and was registered on the Open Science Framework (DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/YP8GW); screening, extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment were duplicated independently.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Nine reports representing eight independent cohorts were included. Protocols were markedly heterogeneous in wavelength (635-940 nm), energy density (5-300 J/cm²), number of sessions, and follow-up, precluding quantitative synthesis. Pain decreased from baseline in most PBM groups, but placebo groups often improved comparably and between-group superiority was less consistent: three of five myogenous cohorts favored PBM and two did not. Only one trial prespecified myalgia and arthralgia as separate strata, favoring PBM for arthralgia but not myalgia. No trial reported the complete World Association for Laser Therapy (WALT) parameter set. Certainty was low for myogenous and very low for arthrogenous TMD.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Photobiomodulation demonstrates pain reduction superior to sham controls in several myogenous TMD trials. However, due to low GRADE certainty and evidence inconsistency, it should be considered a complementary treatment option rather than a standalone therapy.

abstract.label: CLINICAL RELEVANCE
abstract.text: TMD affects approximately 31% of adults and is a leading cause of chronic orofacial pain. PBM was safe, noninvasive, and free of reported adverse effects, and may be considered an adjunct within a conservative, multimodal plan for myogenous TMD. Clinicians should be aware that no preferred dosimetric protocol is established, that the joint-pain evidence rests on one small subgroup, and that placebo responses were substantial. PBM should not displace established conservative measures, and patients should be counseled that the expected benefit over placebo remains uncertain.

title: Sleep, inflammation, and pain in musculoskeletal rehabilitation: a structured integrative review of neurobiological mechanisms and non-pharmacological pain management strategies.
first_affiliation: Faculty of Physical Education, Universidade Estadual de Campinas - UNICAMP, Campinas, São Paulo, Brazil.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Sleep disturbance, inflammation, and persistent pain may reinforce one another, compromising musculoskeletal rehabilitation.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To synthesize evidence on mechanisms linking sleep, inflammation, and pain and identify relevant non-pharmacological interventions.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This structured integrative review examined peer-reviewed studies published from January 2010 to December 2025, identified through PubMed, Scopus, PEDro, and SciELO. Reporting and synthesis were guided by SANRA and EQUATOR recommendations.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Fifty-seven studies were included: 24 experimental or observational studies, 17 systematic reviews or meta-analyses, and 16 narrative or integrative reviews. Sleep restriction was associated with changes in interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor-α, and C-reactive protein, with responses varying across populations and protocols. Prostaglandins and bradykinin may promote nociceptive sensitization, while disrupted sleep may impair descending pain inhibition. Exercise, manual therapy, neuromuscular electrical stimulation, low-level laser therapy, and sleep-focused behavioral interventions showed mechanistic plausibility, although confirmatory trials remain limited.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Sleep assessment and sleep-focused interventions should be considered within multimodal musculoskeletal pain management, while further controlled research clarifies clinical effectiveness.

title: Comparative Effects of Three Active Laser Therapy Protocols and a Sham Protocol on Neurophysiological and Functional Outcomes in Patients with Bell's Palsy: A Four-Arm Randomized Controlled Trial.
first_affiliation: Madina Cardiac Center, Madina 41311, Saudi Arabia.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: Although laser therapy is commonly used to manage Bell's palsy, optimal treatment parameters have not been established. The present randomized controlled trial compared three active laser therapy protocols with a sham-control protocol for neurophysiological and functional recovery in patients with acute Bell's palsy. Methods: The primary analysis included all 104 randomized participants (26 per group) and used multiple imputation for missing six-week outcomes, followed by baseline-adjusted pooled treatment comparisons. In this four-arm trial (NCT07519421), 104 patients were randomized (26 per group) to receive either a sham laser, 808 nm low-level laser therapy (LLLT), 980 nm LLLT, or 1064 nm high-intensity laser therapy (HILT). All participants received standard care, including corticosteroids, electrical stimulation, and facial exercises. Interventions were administered three times per week for six weeks. Compound muscle action potential (CMAP) amplitude was the primary outcome; distal motor latency and the physical and social Facial Disability Index subscales (PFDI/SFDI) were additional outcomes. Eighty patients (20 per group) completed the six-week assessment and constituted the supporting complete-case analysis population. Results: In the primary intention-to-treat analysis, overall between-group differences were significant for CMAP amplitude (Wald χ2(3) = 1844.49), distal motor latency (χ2(3) = 284.90), PFDI (χ2(3) = 359.44), and SFDI (χ2(3) = 842.37; all p < 0.001). The Group C complete treatment protocol was superior to the sham, Group A, and Group B protocols on all four six-week outcomes in Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons (all p < 0.001). The 80-participant complete-case analysis supported the general direction of these findings. An additional baseline-adjusted complete-case sensitivity analysis showed broadly concordant treatment estimates and pairwise inference. No adverse events were reported. Conclusions: Among the complete treatment protocols evaluated, the 1064 nm HILT protocol was associated with the greatest short-term improvements at six weeks. Because the active protocols differed in multiple treatment parameters beyond wavelength, these findings should not be interpreted as demonstrating superiority of the 1064 nm wavelength itself. Longer-term multicenter trials are needed to confirm durability and generalizability. The ITT estimates rely on a missing-at-random assumption for the 24 participants without six-week outcome assessments. Post-imputation diagnostic checks identified departures from regression assumptions, particularly for functional outcomes; inferential results should therefore be interpreted cautiously.
